name: Chapati / Phulka
subtitle: everyday wholewheat flatbread that puffs into a ball over the flame

ingredients.note: omit to keep it vegan and dairy-free; a phulka is dry anyway

prepNotes: Four ingredients and no margin for error: the whole dish is dough hydration and heat.
The dough should be soft enough to take a fingerprint without resistance. Most home chapatis fail because the dough is too stiff.

steps.text: Mix the atta and salt, then add warm water a little at a time, bringing it together into a soft dough.
steps.tip: Soft. If it feels firm, it is already too dry.

steps.text: Knead 8 minutes until smooth and springy, then cover and rest 30 minutes.
steps.tip: Resting relaxes the gluten. Skip it and the rounds fight back as you roll.

steps.text: Divide into 8, roll each into a 16cm round of even thickness, dusting sparingly.
steps.tip: Even thickness matters more than a perfect circle. A thin patch stops the puff.

steps.text: Cook on a hot tawa 30 seconds, until small bubbles appear, then flip.
After another 30 seconds, lift it onto a direct flame with tongs. It should balloon in a few seconds.
steps.tip: If it will not puff, the tawa was not hot enough or the round has a thin spot.

steps.text: Brush with ghee if you want a chapati, leave it dry for a phulka, and stack under a cloth.

storage: Best hot. They keep a few hours under a cloth and go leathery in the fridge. Dough keeps 24 hours refrigerated and rolls better cold.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
